newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ steepens curve on Kiwi bonds after market moves.
newsitem.headline: NZ steepens curve on Kiwi bonds after market moves.

text.p: The New Zealand Debt Management Office, part of the country's Treasury, said on Friday it was cutting the coupon rates on short-term retail Kiwi bonds of six months and one year and raising the interest rate on its two and four-year bond products.
As of May 23, it said following changes would take place -
* Six month rate down 1.25 percentage points to 6.50
* One year rate down 0.50 percentage points to 6.75
* Two-year rate up 0.25 percentage points to 7.00
* Four-year rate up 0.50 percentage points to 7.25 percent.
The DMO said in a statement that the change was based on moving averages of domestic debt market wholesale rates.
"These changes are in response to recent changes in wholesale-market interest rates," it said.
The rates above apply to purchases of at least NZ$5,000, up to a maximum of $250,000.
For small subscriptions of up to NZ$4,900 a set of rates exactly 50 basis points lower apply, and these have also been adjusted by identical margins, the DMO said.
